steady.basis: per IT MW: $20m revenue (the 2029 vintage; the ramp's 2027 vintage is $18m and the 2030 fleet average $18.0m; $20m is the low end of Q2-26 signings), 55% EBITDA (AI cloud 50% in Q2-26; a flat 55% from 2026H2 in the quarterly table overstates the next four quarters by ~$1/share against the ~40% group guide, and is kept for simplicity), GPUs + ancillaries $30m, shell $6m blended (75% owned at $8m), tray-swap refresh 55% of GPU cost every four years plus 3%/yr spares, 21% tax, 10.5% WACC; market $/MW +6%/yr for five years then flat; contracted MW reprice at 2-yr renewals (1-3 yr mid-term book), short-term at 13%; 90/10 blend

finance.basis: debt 7% (first secured facility $775m at SOFR+250; converts 0.5-4.5% cash coupons with accreting principal), 16%/yr pool amortisation, $3bn cash floor; lenders advance 90% of GPUs and 65% of owned shell on contracted capacity, 50% on spot; 10% of capex from 2027 as policy equity at $250 plus the residual; eight convertible series at original principal $13.4bn, accreting to $15.7bn at maturity (post-Aug-26 exchange: 2029/2031 $0.175bn at $51.45; Sep-30/Sep-32 $3.16bn at $138.75; Mar-31/Mar-33 $4.34bn at $183.22/$180.31; Feb-30/Aug-34 $5.75bn at $313.46/$324.65; no capped calls) convert at the model 2030 price; restricted cash ~$1.1bn counted; fully diluted before converts 321.7m = 271.9m basic (30 Jun) + 15.8m Aug exchange + 21.1m NVIDIA pre-funded warrant + 6.2m RSUs + 6.7m options; non-core stakes (ClickHouse ~28%, Avride, Toloka, TripleTen) at the tracker mark of $5.8bn added to equity; opening cash $13.8bn = $8.04bn at 30 Jun (Q2-26 6-K) + $5.75bn August converts; restricted cash $1.056bn (cash-flow statement; $830m in other current assets)

notes: 5 GW contracted, >75% owned. Guidance stepped from >1 GW (Aug-25) to 5 GW (Aug-26) in a year. Owned greenfields: Mäntsälä and Lappeenranta (Finland, 455 MW), Independence MO (1.2 GW, groundbreaking May-26), Pennsylvania (1.2 GW, from 2027), Alabama. Leased: Vineland build-to-suit (Microsoft, 300 MW), Paris, Iceland, Kansas City, UK, Israel, Estonia, France, Spain.Q2-26 letter · 20-F · site releases

Connected lags contracted by ~3 years. Nearly all 5 GW is expected online over 3–3.5 years; 800 MW–1 GW connected by end-2026. The 2025 targets: 100 MW active was beaten (~170 MW), 220 MW connected was never reported against.Q2-26 call · Q4-25 letter

Power is behind the meter at Vineland. Bloom Energy fuel cells (~250 MW guaranteed for 2026) and, per a thermal-drone investigation, dozens of gas generators running since Oct-25; Phase 2 approved Aug-26 lifts the campus to ~350 MW.Bloom partnership May-26 · Floodlight/Guardian 27 Aug · Vineland Planning Board 18 Aug
~270k GPUs by Dec 2026 on ~670 MW active. Finland’s 75 MW hosts Europe’s first GB300 NVL72; Microsoft’s nine Vineland tranches are GB300.Q1-26 letter · Microsoft 6-K
Five-year book life. Servers were depreciated over four years until Jan-26 (“conservative”), then five; the change cut H1-26 depreciation by $86m.20-F FY25 · Q2-26 6-K

Vera Rubin from early 2027. Meta’s $12bn dedicated capacity is one of the first large-scale Vera Rubin deployments, delivery H1-27; the $15bn backstop lets Nebius sell that capacity to others with Meta taking what is unsold.6-K 16 Mar 2026 · Q1-26 letter

ARR on Nebius’s definition. Last month’s AI-cloud revenue × 12: $1.25bn at Dec-25 (guide $0.9–1.1bn), $7–9bn guided for Dec-26. RPO $37.5bn at 30 June, 36% within 24 months; >$40bn of commitments in total. The chart is the model’s contracted run-rate on connected capacity, which runs ahead of the ARR print by one to two quarters.Q2-26 6-K · 12 Aug letter

The book repriced in a year. 2026 base ~$12m per MW; Q2-26 landmark deals (Reflection, Cohere, a US neolab, a quant firm) at $20–25m on 1–3 yr terms; the first capacity auction cleared 15% above any prior Blackwell price; short-term 3–6 month deals at $40–50m. Older-generation pricing rose >30% in the quarter.Q2-26 letter and call

Signed vs contracted. Microsoft ($17.4bn), Meta ($2.9bn + $12bn firm) and the 2026 enterprise book are signed; every owned megawatt from 2027 is assumed to sign at $18–21m per MW as it connects, 10% kept for short-term.90% of unsigned capacity contracted

Prepayments do the funding. ~70% of Q2-26 deals carried prepayments covering 50–60% of capex; >$9bn expected in 2026; Microsoft prepaid $6.96bn of $17.4bn. Deferred revenue $6.0bn at 30 June.Q2-26 letter · 20-F Note on Microsoft

Converts, then secured debt. Four convertible raises in 14 months — $1.0bn (Jun-25), $3.16bn (Sep-25), $4.34bn (Mar-26), $5.75bn (Aug-26); $13.4bn outstanding at original principal, accreting to $15.7bn, no capped calls — plus NVIDIA’s $2bn pre-funded warrant, a $1.15bn follow-on at $92.50 and $2.8bn of ATM at $223.60. The first secured GPU facility ($775m, SOFR+250) closed July-26; management expects “mid-single-digit billions” more against >$40bn of IG-backed contracts.6-Ks · 17 Jul 2026 release

The catch: prepayments and gearing follow signed contracts; the owned greenfields ($8m shell per MW) are built ahead of signing. Unsigned capacity needs ~$19m of equity per MW, and the ATM has 12.3m shares left.funding stack above · Q2-26 6-K

Margins are still climbing. AI-cloud adjusted EBITDA margin 19% (Q3-25) → 24% → 45% → 50% (Q2-26) as co-location and lease costs fall as a share of revenue; group guide ~40% for 2026. Owned campuses at Finland-style PUE 1.13 should take it toward the owner-operator 65%.quarterly 6-Ks · Q4-25 call

Capex is $30m of GPUs per MW plus $8m of shell on owned sites. Management’s split: land and power ~1%, data-centre build 18–20%, GPUs ~80%; 2026 guide $20–25bn (raised from $16–20bn in May); H1-26 spent $8.1bn.Q3-25 call · Q1-26 and Q2-26 letters

Payback 1 year 10 months on Q2-26 deals (was 2–3 years), on prepayments of 50–60% of capex. Maintenance as a tray swap at 55% of GPU cost every four years plus 3%/yr spares: $5.0m per MW-yr on $30m of silicon.Q2-26 letter · model

Some equity, not none. $6.9bn of equity-linked capital in 2026 (NVIDIA warrant, ATM) against $20–25bn of capex. Base: 10% of the 2027–30 build plus the residual the flywheel cannot cover, at an assumed $250 — the bridge shows the count.6-Ks · 12 Aug letter

The multiple is the swing. At $20m per MW and 55% EBITDA, $1 of run-rate is worth ~3.3× — between CoreWeave’s tenant 2.75× and IREN’s owner-operator 4.06×, because Nebius owns most of its shell but pays more for silicon per dollar of revenue on shorter contracts. Signed contracts never escalate; they reprice when they end.contracted 2-yr at 10.5% · short-term at 13%
EPS is the long-run anchor. Non-core stakes (ClickHouse ~28%, Avride, Toloka, TripleTen) are added to equity at the tracker’s $5.8bn mark, not to EV. Pick your multiple.after the raise

footer.model: Compute/Value tracker, Nebius ramp drafted 4 Sep 2026 by the §6e playbook. Ramp: connected/active power as billing IT MW; 2026 to the connected guide, 2027 the owned greenfields, 2028-30 the 5 GW contracted book at ~1 GW a year to 4.7 GW; rates $12.5m per MW-yr on 2026 vintages rising to $21m on 2030, 10% of unsigned capacity at $35m spot, 90% contracted. Capex per MW: $30m Blackwell, +10% on 2027 orders, $38m Rubin, $45m next-gen; shell $8m on owned campuses, none on co-location. Steady-state: $20m revenue per MW-yr, 55% EBITDA, $30m GPUs + $6m blended shell, 21% tax, 10.5% WACC; market $/MW +6%/yr for five years then flat; contracted MW reprice at 2-yr renewals, short-term at 13%; refresh 55% of GPU cost every four years plus 3%/yr; 10% of the 2027–30 build in equity at $250; operating cash funds the build first, prepayments next, debt within lenders’ cover, equity for the rest. Honest-base items: prepayments credited pro rata through reduced instalments with the balance owed at 2030 deducted at PV; eight convertible series as equity at the model’s 2030 price (no capped calls); restricted cash counted; non-core stakes at the tracker mark. Value = 2030 EV less net debt ex converts and prepayments owed, plus non-core, discounted to today, over the diluted count.

capexBasis: GPUs + ancillaries per MW by vintage: $30m Blackwell (derived: 2026 capex guide $20-25bn against ~700 MW added; management: GPUs ~80% of total capex), +10% on 2027 orders, Rubin ~$38m, next-gen ~$45m; shell $8m per MW on owned campuses (management: data-centre build 18-20% of capex), none on co-location
